story_type: Mars landing test: balloon drop, rocket to Mach 4, supersonic parachute tears apart
hook: NASA flew this saucer to the edge of space to watch a parachute rip.
narration: NASA lifted this saucer to the edge of space, lit a rocket, and then watched its parachute rip apart.
It was a test for landing heavy loads on Mars, flown from Hawaii on June twenty eighth, twenty fourteen.
A huge balloon hoisted the seven thousand pound vehicle to one hundred twenty thousand feet.
Then it was released, spun up, and a solid rocket pushed it past four times the speed of sound.
Mars air is about one percent as thick as Earth's, so a heavy lander needs extra drag to slow down.
First, an inflatable ring puffed out around the saucer, smooth and even.
Next, a small balloon shot out the back to drag the big new parachute open.
Tears opened almost at once, and the chute shredded in the violent wake behind the saucer.
outcome: The parachute tore apart, and the cameras gave NASA the data it used to prepare two more test flights.
title: Mars parachute shreds at Mach 2.5
description:
On June 28, 2014, NASA's Low-Density Supersonic Decelerator, a saucer-shaped test vehicle, was carried by balloon to 120,000 feet off Hawaii, rocketed past Mach 4, and tested a new inflatable decelerator and a supersonic parachute that tore apart.

facts.claim: June 28 test of technology to land heavier payloads on Mars
facts.source_quote: On June 28th, NASA's Low-Density Supersonic Accelerator Project conducted the first shakeout flight of a new way of testing technologies that will one day be used to land heavier, more massive payloads on the surface of Mars.

facts.claim: Balloon hoisted 7,000 pound vehicle to 120,000 feet
facts.source_quote: We used a large 34 million cubic foot scientific balloon to hoist a 7,000 pound test vehicle to an altitude of 120,000 feet.

facts.claim: Released, spun up, rocket to over Mach 4
facts.source_quote: The test vehicle was then released from the balloon, spun up for stability, and a large solid rocket motor accelerated to over four times the speed of sound and an altitude of 180,000 feet.

facts.claim: Inflatable decelerator inflated uniformly; balloon pulls the parachute
facts.source_quote: We see that inflated very uniformly without disturbing the vehicle too much.

facts.claim: Early tears in the parachute; data for two more tests
facts.source_quote: we see one of the surprising aspects of this test, which is the early onset of tears in the parachute.
